These are my suggested labels for the inspector in [offer_inspector.py:158-171](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/components/offer_inspector.py:158). I picked names that people in any company would understand.

**Eckdaten**

| Current | Suggestion | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CIU | **Branche** | The values are industries, like "Financial Services" or "Public". "CIU" (Customer Industry Unit) is an Arvato term. |
| Key Accounter | **Kundenbetreuer** (or **Account Manager**) | "Key Accounter" is German-made English that only some companies use. "Account Manager" is the common English term. |
| SharePoint | **Dokumente** (or **Ablage**) | This names what the link is for, not the tool. Teams that use Google Drive or Confluence can use it too. |

**Kalkulation** (the heading itself is fine)

| Current | Suggestion | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PT | **Personentage** | Short forms are hard for new users. The longer word still fits in the inspector. |
| Risikopuffer | keep it (or **Puffer**) | Most people already understand it. |
| Gesamt-PT | **Gesamtaufwand** (or **Personentage gesamt**) | It reads naturally and has no short form. |
| HK | **Kosten** (or **Selbstkosten**) | "Herstellkosten" is a manufacturing term and does not fit service projects well. "Kosten" is the clearest word next to price and margin. |
| Empfohlener VK | **Empfohlener Preis** | "VK" is accounting shorthand. "Preis" means the same thing to everyone. |
| Marge | keep it | It is already a common word. |

**Keep the labels the same everywhere.** The same labels are also used in [offer_table.py:42-46](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/components/offer_table.py:42), [offer_modal.py:59-74](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/components/offer_modal.py:59) and the "HK" group in [price_list.py:27](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/price_list.py:27). If only the inspector changes, the table will say "HK" while the inspector says "Kosten". I would put the labels in shared constants in `alloq_offer`, so every view uses the same words.

The option names in `CIU_LABELS` (for example "Financial Services - FS") still end with Arvato codes. Under the label "Branche" they would read better as just "Finanzdienstleistungen", "Öffentlicher Sektor" and so on. That is a separate choice, because those values are also used to pick the industry in the offer form.

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

def apply_state_change(
    state: str,  # noqa: ARG001
    sent_date: date | None,
    new_state: str,
    today: date,
) -> date | None:
    """Sent date after moving to ``new_state``.

    Moving to "Versendet" without a date sets ``today``; every other change
    keeps the date, also when moving back to an earlier state.
    """
    if new_state == OfferStateEnum.SENT and sent_date is None:
        return today
    return sent_date


def total_days(offer: Offer) -> Decimal:
    """Person days plus risk buffer."""
    return offer.person_days + offer.risk_buffer_days


def margin_pct(offer: Offer) -> Decimal | None:
    """Margin in percent of the recommended price; None when it is 0."""
    if not offer.recommended_price:
        return None
    return (
        (offer.recommended_price - offer.production_cost)
        / offer.recommended_price
        * 100
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OfferTotals:
    """Footer sums of a list of offers."""

    person_days: Decimal = Decimal(0)
    production_cost: Decimal = Decimal(0)
    recommended_price: Decimal = Decimal(0)


def totals(offers: list[Offer]) -> OfferTotals:
    """Sum of PT (incl. buffer), HK and VK."""
    return OfferTotals(
        person_days=sum((total_days(o) for o in offers), Decimal(0)),
        production_cost=sum((o.production_cost for o in offers), Decimal(0)),
        recommended_price=sum((o.recommended_price for o in offers), Decimal(0)),
    )


def search_offers(offers: list[Offer], query: str) -> list[Offer]:
    """Offers whose title, customer or key accounter contain ``query``."""
    needle = query.strip().casefold()
    if not needle:
        return list(offers)
    return [
        o
        for o in offers
        if needle in o.title.casefold()
        or needle in o.customer.casefold()
        or needle in o.key_accounter.casefold()
    ]


def filter_offers(offers: list[Offer], list_filter: str) -> list[Offer]:
    """Apply a filter segment; archived offers show only under "Archiviert"."""
    if list_filter == FILTER_ARCHIVED:
        return [o for o in offers if o.archived]
    active = [o for o in offers if not o.archived]
    if list_filter in GROUP_ORDER:
        return [o for o in active if o.state == list_filter]

) -> None:
    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
    metadata = sa.MetaData()
    users = sa.Table(
        "auth_users",
        metadata,
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("is_admin", sa.Boolean),
        sa.Column("roles", sa.String),
    )
    rows = [
        (1, True, "[]"),

        (3, True, '["employee", "offer_editor"]'),
        (4, False, '["offer_editor"]'),
        (5, False, "[]"),

    with engine.begin() as conn:

        conn.execute(
            users.insert(),
            [{"id": i, "is_admin": a, "roles": r} for i, a, r in rows],

        _run(role_grant, "upgrade", conn)

"""Move the offer CIU codes into an editable industries (Branchen) table.

Seeds one industry per former CIU code, links every offer through
``industry_id`` and drops the ``ciu`` column. Codes outside the known six
become an industry named after the code, so no offer loses its value.

Revision ID: f1a2b3c4d5e6
Revises: e023b4c5d6f7
Create Date: 2026-10-21 15:00:00.000000
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

import sqlalchemy as sa

from alembic import op

revision: str = "f1a2b3c4d5e6"
down_revision: str | None = "e023b4c5d6f7"
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None

INDUSTRIES: dict[str, str] = {
    "CP": "Verbraucherdienstleistungen",
    "FS": "Finanzdienstleistungen",
    "U": "Energie und Versorgung",
    "P": "Öffentlicher Sektor",
    "H": "Gesundheitswesen",
    "IMC": "Industrie und Mittelstand",
}
"""Former CIU code -> industry name."""

FK_NAME = "fk_offers_industry_id_industries"
INDEX_NAME = "ix_offers_industry_id"


def upgrade() -> None:
    industries = op.create_table(
        "industries",
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer(), primary_key=True, autoincrement=True),
        sa.Column(
            "created",
            sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
            server_default=sa.func.now(),
            nullable=False,
        ),
        sa.Column(
            "updated",
            sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
            server_default=sa.func.now(),
            nullable=False,
        ),
        sa.Column("name", sa.String(100), nullable=False, unique=True),
    )
    conn = op.get_bind()
    unknown = [
        code
        for (code,) in conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT DISTINCT ciu FROM offers"))
        if code not in INDUSTRIES
    ]
    names = {**INDUSTRIES, **{code: code for code in unknown}}
    op.bulk_insert(industries, [{"name": name} for name in names.values()])

    with op.batch_alter_table("offers") as batch:
        batch.add_column(sa.Column("industry_id", sa.Integer(), nullable=True))
    for code, name in names.items():
        conn.execute(
            sa.text(
                "UPDATE offers SET industry_id = "
                "(SELECT id FROM industries WHERE name = :name) WHERE ciu = :code"
            ),
            {"name": name, "code": code},
        )
    with op.batch_alter_table("offers") as batch:
        batch.alter_column("industry_id", existing_type=sa.Integer(), nullable=False)
        batch.create_foreign_key(
            FK_NAME, "industries", ["industry_id"], ["id"], ondelete="RESTRICT"
        )
        batch.create_index(INDEX_NAME, ["industry_id"])
        batch.drop_column("ciu")


def downgrade() -> None:
    """Restore the codes; industries added later keep their first 10 chars."""
    conn = op.get_bind()
    with op.batch_alter_table("offers") as batch:
        batch.add_column(sa.Column("ciu", sa.String(10), nullable=True))
    codes = {name: code for code, name in INDUSTRIES.items()}
    rows = conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT id, name FROM industries")).all()
    for industry_id, name in rows:
        conn.execute(
            sa.text("UPDATE offers SET ciu = :code WHERE industry_id = :id"),
            {"code": codes.get(name, name[:10]), "id": industry_id},
        )
    with op.batch_alter_table("offers") as batch:
        batch.alter_column("ciu", existing_type=sa.String(10), nullable=False)
        batch.drop_index(INDEX_NAME)
        batch.drop_constraint(FK_NAME, type_="foreignkey")
        batch.drop_column("industry_id")
    op.drop_table("industries")

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.components.dialogs import delete_dialog
from alloq_commons.components.forms import section
from alloq_commons.components.modal_layout import (
    MODAL_CLASS,
    modal_footer,
    modal_form_layout,
)
from alloq_commons.components.toolbar import primary_button, toolbar_search
from reflex.event import EventType
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_offer.models import Industry
from alloq_offer.states.industry_state import IndustryState
from appkit_ui.styles import sticky_header_style

NAME_HINT = "Wird im Angebot unter „Branche“ zur Auswahl angeboten."


def industry_form_fields(industry: ObjectVar[Industry] | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    return section(
        mn.text_input(
            name="name",
            label="Name",
            description=NAME_HINT,
            default_value=industry.name if industry is not None else "",
            placeholder="z.B. Finanzdienstleistungen",
            required=True,
            custom_attrs={"maxLength": 100},
            left_section=rx.icon("factory", size=16),
        ),
    )


def _industry_modal(
    *,
    title: str,
    opened: rx.Var[bool],
    on_close: EventType[()],
    on_submit: EventType[Any],
    content: rx.Component,
) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.modal(
        modal_form_layout(
            content=mn.flex(
                content,
                mn.space(height="2rem"),
                direction="column",
                width="100%",
            ),
            footer=modal_footer("Branche speichern", on_close),
            on_submit=on_submit,
        ),
        title=title,
        opened=opened,
        on_close=on_close,
        size="md",
        centered=True,
        class_name=MODAL_CLASS,
        overlay_props={"backgroundOpacity": 0.5, "blur": 4},
    )


def add_industry_modal() -> rx.Component:
    return _industry_modal(
        title="Branche hinzufügen",
        opened=IndustryState.add_modal_open,
        on_close=IndustryState.close_add_modal,
        on_submit=IndustryState.create_industry,
        content=industry_form_fields(),
    )


def edit_industry_modal() -> rx.Component:
    return _industry_modal(
        title="Branche bearbeiten",
        opened=IndustryState.edit_modal_open,
        on_close=IndustryState.close_edit_modal,
        on_submit=IndustryState.update_industry,
        content=mn.box(
            industry_form_fields(IndustryState.selected_industry.to(Industry)),
            key=IndustryState.selected_industry.to(Industry).id.to(str),
        ),
    )


def _row(industry: ObjectVar[Industry]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.table.tr(
        mn.table.td(mn.text(industry.name, size="sm", fw="500")),
        mn.table.td(
            mn.group(
                rx.icon_button(
                    rx.icon("square-pen", size=16),
                    on_click=IndustryState.open_edit_modal(industry.id),
                    variant="ghost",
                ),
                delete_dialog(
                    title="Löschen bestätigen",
                    content=industry.name,
                    on_click=IndustryState.delete_industry(industry.id),
                    icon_button=True,
                    color="red",
                    variant="subtle",
                ),
                gap="xs",
                wrap="nowrap",
                align="center",
            ),
            width="1%",
            style={"whiteSpace": "nowrap"},
        ),
    )


def _loading_row() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.table.tr(
        mn.table.td(
            rx.hstack(
                rx.spinner(size="3"),
                mn.text("Lade Branchen...", size="sm"),
                align="center",
                justify="center",
                spacing="3",
            ),
            col_span=2,
            style={"textAlign": "center"},
        ),
    )


def industries_table() -> rx.Component:
    """List of industries with add, edit and delete."""
    return mn.stack(
        add_industry_modal(),
        edit_industry_modal(),
        mn.table(
            mn.table.thead(
                mn.table.tr(
                    mn.table.th(mn.text("Name", size="sm", fw="700")),
                    mn.table.th(mn.text("", size="sm")),
                    style=sticky_header_style,
                ),
            ),
            mn.table.tbody(
                rx.cond(
                    IndustryState.is_loading,
                    _loading_row(),
                    rx.foreach(IndustryState.filtered_industries, _row),
                )
            ),
            sticky_header=True,
            sticky_header_offset="0px",
            highlight_on_hover=True,
            highlight_on_hover_color=rx.color_mode_cond(
                light="gray.0",
                dark="dark.8",
            ),
            w="100%",
        ),
        w="100%",
    )


def industries_toolbar() -> list[rx.Component]:
    """Toolbar actions of the industries page."""
    return [
        toolbar_search(
            IndustryState.search_filter,
            IndustryState.set_search_filter,
            "Branchen suchen",
        ),
        primary_button("Neue Branche", "plus", IndustryState.open_add_modal),
    ]

# Offers

This page covers the page "Angebote" [offers] at `/offers`. It lists the offers that the company calculated for customer projects, with person days, risk buffer, production cost and recommended price. The stories belong to the activity "Prepare offers" on the [story map](./story-map.md).

The page has four user tasks:

- **Find an offer.** Read the list grouped by status, search, filter and sort it, and read one offer in the inspector.
- **Create an offer.** Enter a new offer in the form "Neues Angebot" [new offer].
- **Maintain an offer.** Edit an offer, change its status and sent date in the inspector, and archive or restore it.
- **Give access to offers.** An admin gives a user the role "Angebote" [offers].

An offer is one row in `OfferEntity` (table `offers`). All values are typed in by hand. Alloq does not calculate them from daily rates, and an offer is not linked to a project. Offers are never deleted. The package has no delete handler, and an offer that is no longer needed is archived.

Admins, project managers and users with the role `offer_editor` can open the page and change offers. In this page the persona "Offer editor" means all three. Every data handler has the guard `requires_offer_editor`. The code lives in the independent package `components/alloq-offer`, which imports only `alloq-commons` and appkit.

Offer editor · Find an offer / Read the list · priority 1 · core · unreleased

### Acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a user who may edit offers, **when** they open `/offers`, **then** `load_offers` loads all offers with the newest change first. The loader shows only on the first load, and later loads keep the list on screen.
2. **Given** the loaded offers, **when** the table renders, **then** it shows the columns "Angebot" [offer] with title and customer, "Key Accounter", "CIU", "Status", "PT" [person days], "HK" [production cost], "VK" [sales price] and "Versendet am" [sent on].
3. **Given** active offers, **when** the table renders, **then** they appear in the groups "Neu" [new], "In Bearbeitung" [in progress] and "Versendet" [sent], in this order, and a group without offers is hidden. Each status has its own badge colour.
4. **Given** an offer, **when** its row renders, **then** "PT" shows person days plus risk buffer, "HK" and "VK" show euros with two decimals, and "Versendet am" shows the date as DD.MM.YYYY or "–" when there is none.
5. **Given** the visible offers, **when** the footer row "Summe" [sum] renders, **then** it shows the sums of PT (with buffer), HK and VK of exactly the visible rows.

description: ORDER BY name in the alloq Postgres puts Ö/Ä/Ü after Z; sort German names in Python

The alloq Postgres sorts by byte order, so `ORDER BY name` lists "Öffentlicher Sektor" after "Verbraucher…" (seen 2026-10-21 on the industries page). SQLite in tests hides this.

**Why:** admins read these lists alphabetically; umlauts at the end look like a bug.
**How to apply:** for German display names, sort in Python with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name).casefold()` as key (see `IndustryRepository.find_all_ordered`), and add an umlaut name to the repository test.

description: PROFILES=local points at a remote (.tech) Postgres, not a local DB; migrations there are shared

`.env` has `PROFILES=local`, but the DB host secret is a remote server (`*.tech`), not localhost. `uv run alembic current` reads that DB. On 2026-10-21 the industries migration `f1a2b3c4d5e6` was already applied there a few minutes after the file was written; I never ran `alembic upgrade`, and Reflex does not migrate on `reflex run`.

**Why:** a new migration changes a shared database, and dropping a column there cannot be undone without the downgrade.
**How to apply:** never run `alembic upgrade`/`downgrade` yourself; ask the user. Check `alembic current` before a browser check, so you know whether the running app has the new schema. Related: [[local-test-login]], [[local-visual-check-browser]].

Lint, typecheck and all 1605 tests pass, with 90.6% coverage. I also opened the admin page, the offers table, the inspector and the edit form in the running app, and all of them work.

**Important: your shared database already has the new schema.** Your local profile connects to a remote database, not a local one. That database is already at the new migration `f1a2b3c4d5e6`. I did not run `alembic upgrade`, and Reflex does not run migrations when it starts, so I can't tell what applied it. It happened a few minutes after I wrote the migration file. That database now has the six industries, every offer is linked to one, and the old `ciu` column is gone. If that was too early, `alembic downgrade e023b4c5d6f7` puts the codes back.

**New labels**
- In the inspector:
  - "Branche"
  - "Account Manager"
  - "Dokumente"
  - "Personentage"
  - "Risikopuffer"
  - "Gesamtaufwand"
  - "Kosten"
  - "Empfohlener Preis"
  - "Marge"
- The offer table, the form and the search placeholder use the same words. The table columns are "Personentage", "Kosten" and "Preis".
- Number values still end with "PT", for example "140 PT". The label above them now explains the short form. Say if you want "Tage" instead.

**Editable industries**
- A new `industries` table replaces the fixed CIU codes. Offers point to it through `industry_id`.
- The migration created six German names from the old codes:
  - Verbraucherdienstleistungen
  - Finanzdienstleistungen
  - Energie und Versorgung
  - Öffentlicher Sektor
  - Gesundheitswesen
  - Industrie und Mittelstand

- An industry that offers still use can't be deleted. Archived offers count too. The app shows a message, and the database also refuses the delete.
- The industry list is sorted by name, with umlauts next to their base letter. Before the fix, "Öffentlicher Sektor" showed up last.
